description: The Account settings tab (reached via the 'settings-account' sidebar entry or the 'settings' tab which defaults to 'account') displays user authentication status and runner-to-cloud connection configuration. It renders four sections: (1) a Connection section header with description; (2) a conditionally-shown User Info card with email, optional display name, and a Sign Out button; (3) a Runner Identity section with a persistent text input for the runner's display name; (4) a conditionally-shown Project Selection dropdown (only when projects are available); and (5) Connection Controls with a Connect/Disconnect button, real-time WebSocket status badge, and a device/URL info panel. The page manages the runner's link to qontinui.io for real-time monitoring and cloud storage. No visible tab bar is rendered here — sub-tab switching happens via the sidebar.

groups.name: Page Structure
groups.description: The Account settings page renders within the shared Settings container (data-page-id='settings'). It is a vertically scrollable single-column layout with a Connection section header at the top followed by stacked card-style sections.

assertions.description: A 'Connection' heading is visible at the top of the Account tab content
The description text 'Connect your runner to qontinui.io for real-time monitoring and cloud storage.' appears below the Connection heading

criteria.textContent: Connect your runner to qontinui.io for real-time monitoring and cloud storage.

assertions.description: A 'Runner Identity' sub-section heading is present on the page
A 'Connection Status' sub-section heading is present on the page

groups.name: User Info Card — Authenticated State
groups.description: When the user is authenticated, a card showing their email address and optional display name is rendered. A 'Sign Out' button with a destructive/red style appears on the right side of this card. This section is NOT rendered when unauthenticated.

assertions.description: The user's email address is displayed with data-content-label='user email'

The element with data-content-label='user email' contains a non-empty email address string (e.g., 'user@example.com'). An empty or missing value indicates the auth status failed to populate user data.
A 'Sign Out' button is present in the user info card

If the authenticated user has a display name, it appears with data-content-label='user name' below the email in a smaller muted style. If the user has no name, this element is absent. The name is optional in the user profile.
When the user is NOT authenticated, the Sign Out button is not rendered (the entire user info card is absent)
assertions.precondition: User is not authenticated (not logged in)

groups.name: Sign Out Behavior
groups.description: Clicking Sign Out disconnects the WebSocket (if connected) then calls the Tauri logout command to clear tokens from the OS keychain and deactivate the device on the backend. After success the user info card disappears.

assertions.description: Clicking the 'Sign Out' button (1) disconnects any active WebSocket connection, (2) calls the Tauri 'logout' command which deactivates the device via DELETE /api/v1/runner-devices/{device_id} and clears tokens from the OS keychain, (3) logs 'Logged out successfully' as a success message, and (4) removes the user info card from the UI so the Sign Out button is no longer visible. If an error occurs, an error message 'Logout failed: ...' is logged instead.

groups.name: Runner Identity Section
groups.description: The Runner Identity section contains a text input for the runner's display name. The name is stored to localStorage (key: 'qontinui-runner-name') on every keystroke without requiring a Save button. The stored name is also dispatched via a 'runner-name-changed' CustomEvent to notify the StatusIndicator component.

assertions.description: A 'Runner Name' label is present above the name input
A text input with placeholder 'My Runner' is present in the Runner Identity section
Helper text containing the phrase 'identify it on qontinui.io' is visible below the Runner Name label

Typing a name into the Runner Name input immediately stores it in localStorage under key 'qontinui-runner-name' and dispatches a 'runner-name-changed' CustomEvent. The stored value persists across page reloads and is restored as the input's value on mount. No Save button is required — persistence is automatic on each keystroke.

groups.name: Project Selection Section
groups.description: The Project Selection section is only rendered when projects.length > 0. It shows a dropdown button that opens a list of available projects. Project selection is disabled while the WebSocket is connected — the dropdown button becomes non-interactive and displays a hint 'Disconnect to change projects.' Only one project can be selected at a time; the selected project shows a checkmark icon.

assertions.description: A 'Select Project' sub-section heading is present when at least one project is available
assertions.precondition: User is authenticated and at least one project exists

assertions.description: The 'Select Project' section heading is NOT rendered when no projects are available
assertions.precondition: User is authenticated but no projects exist

assertions.description: A dropdown button showing either the selected project name or the placeholder text 'Select a project...' is present when projects are available
assertions.precondition: At least one project exists and no project is currently selected

assertions.description: Clicking the project dropdown button (when not connected) opens a list of available projects. Clicking a project name in the list selects it — the dropdown closes, the button label updates to the project name, and a checkmark icon appears next to that project on the next open. The dropdown cannot be opened while the WebSocket is connected (button is visually dimmed with opacity-60 and does not respond to clicks).
assertions.precondition: At least one project exists and WebSocket is not connected

assertions.description: When the WebSocket is connected, a message 'Disconnect to change projects.' appears below the project dropdown and the dropdown button is visually dimmed and does not open on click
assertions.precondition: User is connected and at least one project exists

groups.name: Connection Controls
groups.description: The Connection Controls section shows either a Connect or Disconnect button depending on the current WebSocket state. The Connect button is disabled if connectionInfo is missing or no project is selected. During connection, a spinner replaces the Wifi icon and the label becomes 'Connecting...'.

assertions.description: A 'Connect' button is present when the WebSocket is not connected
The 'Connect' button is NOT present when the WebSocket is already connected
A 'Disconnect' button is present when the WebSocket is connected
The Connect button is in a disabled state when no project is selected and projects are available. This prevents attempting a connection without a project context.
assertions.precondition: Projects are available but none is selected, and WebSocket is not connected

assertions.description: Clicking the Connect button (1) shows a loading spinner and changes the label to 'Connecting...' while in-progress, (2) invokes the Tauri commands get_access_token_for_websocket, configure_websocket (with token and project ID), and connect_websocket in sequence, (3) on success transitions the button to 'Disconnect' and shows the 'Connected' status badge next to 'Connection Status', (4) starts a device heartbeat at 30-second intervals. If connection fails, the error message section appears with the error text.
assertions.precondition: A project is selected and WebSocket is not connected

assertions.description: Clicking the Disconnect button invokes the Tauri disconnect_websocket command, updates the UI to show the Connect button, removes the 'Connected' status badge, and sets an internal flag that prevents automatic reconnection. The connection info panel remains visible but the WebSocket status within it changes to 'Disconnected'.

groups.name: Connection Status Indicators
groups.description: The Connection Controls section header shows a 'Connected' status badge with an animated pulse dot when the WebSocket is active. This badge has data-content-label='connection connected' and is removed when disconnected.

assertions.description: When connected, a status element with data-content-label='connection connected' containing the text 'Connected' is visible next to the 'Connection Status' heading
The data-content-label='connection connected' element is NOT present when the WebSocket is disconnected
The element with data-content-label='websocket status' shows 'Connected' in green/success color when the WebSocket is active, and 'Disconnected' in orange/amber color when not connected
assertions.precondition: connectionInfo is available (device has been registered)

groups.name: Connection Info Details Panel
groups.description: When connectionInfo is available (i.e., the device has been registered and connection info fetched via GET /api/v1/runner-devices/{device_id}/connection-info), a details panel shows three rows: Device ID (truncated to first 8 characters + '...'), WebSocket URL (truncated to 40 characters + '...'), and WebSocket connection status. This panel is absent before connection info is loaded.

assertions.description: A 'Device ID:' label with data-content-label='device id label' is shown in the connection info panel
The device ID value with data-content-label='device id value' shows a truncated monospace string ending in '...' — the first 8 characters of the device UUID followed by ellipsis
The WebSocket URL value with data-content-label='websocket url value' shows a truncated monospace string ending in '...' — the first 40 characters of the WebSocket endpoint URL

The connection info panel displays data returned by the Tauri get_connection_info command (backed by GET /api/v1/runner-devices/{device_id}/connection-info). The device_id is a UUID shown truncated to 8 chars. The websocket_url is the full WebSocket endpoint shown truncated to 40 chars. The live WebSocket connection state (not the API's is_active field) determines whether the status row shows 'Connected' or 'Disconnected'.

groups.name: Warning and Info Notices
groups.description: Two contextual notices appear in the Connection Controls section. An orange warning appears when projects are available but none is selected. A blue info notice appears when no projects exist (user has not created a project on qontinui.io yet).

assertions.description: An orange-tinted warning box containing 'Please select a project before connecting.' is shown when projects exist but none is selected

criteria.textContent: Please select a project before connecting.

assertions.precondition: At least one project is available but no project is selected

assertions.description: A blue-tinted info box containing 'No projects found. Create a project on qontinui.io first.' is shown when no projects are available

criteria.textContent: No projects found. Create a project on qontinui.io first.

assertions.precondition: User is authenticated but no projects are available

assertions.description: The 'Please select a project before connecting.' warning is NOT shown when a project is currently selected

criteria.textContent: Please select a project before connecting.

groups.name: Connection Error State
groups.description: When a WebSocket connection error occurs, an error banner with red/error styling and an X icon appears between the User Info card and the Runner Identity section. The banner contains the error message string. The banner disappears when there is no error.

assertions.description: When a WebSocket connection error occurs, an error-styled banner appears containing the error message text. The banner uses getStatusColors('error') styling (red background and text). It is absent when no error exists.

target.label: Connection area (error banner appears above Runner Identity)

assertions.precondition: A WebSocket connection error has occurred

groups.name: UI Bridge Component Actions
groups.description: The Settings panel is registered as a UI Bridge component with id 'settings-panel'. It exposes four actions: 'save' (persists the active tab preference), 'reset' (returns to the account tab), 'switch-tab' (changes to any valid settings tab by tabId), and 'list-tabs' (returns all available tab ids and labels). These allow AI automation drivers to control the settings panel programmatically.

assertions.description: The 'switch-tab' UI Bridge action on component 'settings-panel' accepts a tabId parameter and switches the settings panel to that sub-tab. Valid tabIds: account, ai, agentic, self-healing, world-state-verifier, playwright, mobile, cloud-relay, discovery, web-integration, mcp, log-sources, execution-variables, notifications, general, storage, backup, instances, otel, containers, security, advanced, updates. An invalid tabId throws an error listing valid options.

The 'list-tabs' UI Bridge action returns an array of {id, label} for all 23 settings tabs. The account tab entry is {id: 'account', label: 'Account'}. This allows AI drivers to enumerate available sub-tabs without DOM scraping.

states.name: Unauthenticated
states.description: User is not logged in. User info card is absent. Connect button is present but disabled (no connectionInfo). No project section shown. Runner Identity section is present.

states.name: Authenticated — No Projects
states.description: User is logged in but has no projects. User info card shows email and Sign Out button. No project section rendered. Blue info notice 'No projects found' is visible. Connect button is present.

elements.textContent: No projects found. Create a project on qontinui.io first.

states.name: Authenticated — Disconnected
states.description: User is logged in with projects available, WebSocket is not connected. User info card visible. Project dropdown is enabled. Connect button is active (enabled when project is selected). No 'Connected' badge.

transitions.name: Connect to qontinui.io
transitions.description: Click the Connect button to initiate WebSocket connection

transitions.name: Sign Out
transitions.description: Click Sign Out to log out while disconnected

states.name: Authenticated — Connected
states.description: User is logged in and WebSocket is active. 'Connected' badge visible next to 'Connection Status' heading. Connection info panel shows device ID, WebSocket URL, and 'Connected' status. Disconnect button present. Project dropdown is locked (read-only).

transitions.name: Disconnect WebSocket
transitions.description: Click the Disconnect button to terminate the WebSocket connection

transitions.name: Sign Out (while connected)
transitions.description: Click Sign Out — disconnects WebSocket first, then logs out
